title: Your Paycheck In 2027: Will You Get A Raise Or Get Laid Off? | Holly Wade
speaker: Holly Wade (NFIB)

macro_themes.view: NFIB optimism fell 0.8 in September to about the 52-year average of 98, driven by weaker outlook for business conditions and expansion.

macro_themes.theme: Tight labor market for skilled trades
macro_themes.view: Small firms still struggle to find qualified workers, especially construction, manufacturing and specialty trades, partly because data-center construction outbids them.
More owners are having to raise compensation than planned to; wage growth next year likely strongest in expanding services, manufacturing and construction.
Fuel, tariff and labor costs are being absorbed first and eventually passed on to customers, squeezing small business earnings.
Midterm elections, the Iran war and policy changes keep uncertainty high, making owners more conservative on hiring and investment.
AI is augmenting rather than replacing small business staff, mostly filling unfilled roles through attrition.

notes: Economic-survey interview with no market, sector or ticker calls. GRML (Greenland Mines) mentioned only in a paid sponsor read, not a call.
